headline: Steady earnings growth as data-center demand accelerates
summary_short: FirstEnergy reported Q2 2026 GAAP earnings of $288M, or $0.50 per basic and diluted share (+7.5% / +8.7% y/y), on revenue of $3,678M (+8.8% y/y), while reaffirming its FY2026 Core (non-GAAP) EPS guidance range of $2.62-$2.82.
summary_long: Revenue was $3,678M (+8.8% y/y, -12.5% q/q on normal seasonal patterns) and net income rose to $288M (+7.5% y/y, -28.9% q/q); GAAP EPS was $0.50 (+8.7% y/y), matching Core (non-GAAP) EPS of $0.50, down from $0.52 a year ago but 'in line with plan.' By segment: Distribution Core EPS fell $0.06/share y/y on higher maintenance expense; Integrated was flat as 22% transmission rate-base growth offset planned maintenance; Stand-Alone Transmission rose $0.04/share on an 11% rate-base increase. FirstEnergy reaffirmed FY2026 Core EPS guidance of $2.62-$2.82 and its 6%-8% long-term Core EPS CAGR through 2030, backed by a $6B FY2026 capex plan and a $36B five-year Energize365 program (raised ~30% vs. the prior five-year plan) amid accelerating data-center demand.

drivers.explanation: CEO Brian X. Tierney attributed results to continued execution of the regulated investment strategy, cost management, and improved operations, plus accelerating data-center demand (contracted demand +30% since Q1) and growth in West Virginia.

Not itemized separately from the earnings narrative; the release attributes overall results to continued execution of the regulated investment strategy, cost management, and improved operations across the service territory.

Tracks the segment-level GAAP EPS narrative: Distribution fell on higher maintenance costs, Integrated was flat, and Stand-Alone Transmission rose on rate-base growth; net gain reflects that mix plus a $0.02/share smaller net drag from special items y/y.

Segment mix drove the y/y gain: Distribution Core EPS fell $0.06/share on higher maintenance costs; Integrated was flat as 22% transmission rate-base growth offset planned maintenance; Stand-Alone Transmission rose $0.04/share on an 11% rate-base increase.
The release states diluted EPS equals basic EPS this quarter and a year ago ($0.50 and $0.46); the same segment-mix drivers cited for EPS (basic) apply identically.
